_mock: Stand-in until GET /api/gap exists. Bridge values derived from the live /api/overview chart growth_vs_profit (discounts and cost of goods combined, the split is not computed yet). Driver text from docs/PLAN.md.

bridge.label: Extra discounts and cost of goods

drivers.title: Quarter-end discount push (R07, Atlantic resellers)
drivers.what: R07 books 48% of revenue in the last 14 days of each quarter at a 27% average discount (other reps 9 to 12%). 207 orders cross the rule: $892,567 of revenue, $170,676 refunded later.
drivers.why: The quarterly target and bonus pay on gross revenue. Deep discounts land in the last 14 days, and resellers send the overstock back about a month later.
drivers.todo: Pay quota on revenue net of returns after 45 days, and require approval for quarter-end discounts of 25% or more.

drivers.title: Furniture damaged in transit (BC, Prairies)
drivers.what: Damaged-in-transit refunds are 16.9% of furniture revenue in BC and 15.4% in the Prairies, vs 3.8% in Ontario. BC is also the fastest-growing region (+50%).
drivers.why: Big items ship long-haul from Montreal, and the fastest-growing region is the farthest one.
drivers.todo: Change packaging or carrier for long-haul furniture.

drivers.title: Business customers going quiet after a bad return
drivers.what: 70 business customers went quiet ($618,246 of 2025 spend). 59% of them had a damaged, defective or wrong-item return, vs 27% of active customers.
drivers.why: Nobody calls after a bad return, so nobody learns why the customer left.
drivers.todo: Contact every business customer right after a bad return.

drivers.title: Late payments
drivers.what: $135,367 overdue at extraction, 3 customers past 60 days. The late-payment rate is flat since 2025.
drivers.why: Steady since 2025, so it is not what changed.
drivers.todo: Monitor, and put a credit hold only on clear cases.

who_is_right.claim: Revenue up about a third, the Atlantic team punches above its weight
who_is_right.evidence: Top line true (+33%). Atlantic's growth is discounting plus returns; its SMB and Enterprise revenue fell 25%.

who_is_right.claim: Cash is tight, profit is not keeping up, we chase unpaid invoices
who_is_right.evidence: Profit lag true (refunds +67%). Unpaid invoices are real but small: $135k overdue, flat since 2025.

who_is_right.claim: Returns eat warehouse time, especially big items
who_is_right.evidence: Furniture damaged in transit to BC (16.9% of furniture revenue) and the Prairies (15.4%).
70 business customers ($619k in 2025). 59% had a bad return vs 27% of active ones.

why_first:
Ranked on four plain criteria: size in dollars, whether it changed in 2026, whether the company controls it, whether a rule catches it early.
#1 Quarter-end discount push: the largest controllable piece, new in 2026 (R07's discount went from 18-19% in 2025 to 28% in 2026), one cause, and a rule catches it with almost no false alarms. This is what the tool automates first.
#2 Transit damage, then quiet customers: big ($619k of 2025 spend went quiet), but the root fix is operational. The tool handles the customer side (C2).
#3 Late payments: real but flat and smaller ($135k overdue). Monitor only.
